name: recruitment-adversarial
title: Control: no cue, no recruitment
question:
If competent responders are placed with NO cue secreted, does the metric
correctly report no recruitment (rather than a spurious signal)?
hypothesis:
With the response intact (lambda 14) but the cue removed (rate 0), there is no
gradient to climb; the recruitment index stays at zero.
objective:
Run the world with competent responders but the source secretion turned off, and
confirm the recruitment index and metric correctly report no recruitment.
description:
The adversarial / negative-control arm. Responders are fully competent (lambda=14)
but there is no cue (secretion rate 0), so no gradient forms. A trustworthy
recruitment claim must FAIL to fire here — the metric passes by rejecting a system
that should not qualify. This closes the causal logic: recruitment requires BOTH a
cue AND a response, and neither alone suffices.
claim:
Without a cue, competent responders are not recruited: the recruitment index
stays at 0. The metric does not produce a false-positive recruitment signal.
expected_behavior: Recruitment index stays at zero despite responders being chemotaxis-competent.
The metric issues no spurious recruitment signal in the absence of a cue.

embed_visualizations.name: Animated spatial scene
embed_visualizations.title: Chemotactic recruitment — animated scene (baseline vs this condition)

readouts.name: Recruitment index
readouts.description: Fraction of responder cell centres of mass within 15 px of the source centroid.

behavior_tests.name: No cue yields no recruitment (rejection)
behavior_tests.description:
Pass criterion (by rejection): recruitment index stays below 0.1 even though
responders are competent. Measured from the run: recruitment index remains
0.000 across all sweeps — the metric correctly rejects.

evidence.observed: recruitment index 0.000 ± 0.000 across 5 seeds with no cue — the metric issues no spurious recruitment

findings.statement:
Negative control holds: across 5 seeds competent responders are not recruited
without a cue (recruitment index 0.000 +/- 0.000; baseline 0.767, Cohen's d =
6.38), and the metric reports no spurious recruitment.

controls.name: Response blocked (recruitment-inhibited)
controls.description: The other necessary-cause arm — blocking the response also gives no recruitment.

alternative_hypotheses.claim: The recruitment metric fires on responder proximity regardless of a cue.
alternative_hypotheses.note: Excluded here — competent responders with no cue leave the index at 0.

conclusion:
The recruitment claim does not over-generalize. Recruitment is jointly caused by
cue and response; removing either abolishes it. This adversarial arm gives the
investigation its falsification exposure and adversarial coverage.
key_assumptions: Identical world to recruitment-baseline except source secretion rate = 0.

No cue yields no recruitment (rejection).notes: 0.000 across 5 seeds with no cue; the metric correctly rejects
